subject: chemistry
title: Molar gas volume
key_idea: Equal amounts in moles of any gas occupy the same volume at the same temperature and pressure. At room temperature and pressure, one mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³. Use this to link moles, mass and volume of gases.

sections.heading: The molar volume of a gas

blocks.text: (Higher tier, chemistry only) Gas volumes depend on temperature and pressure, so they are compared under the same conditions.

items.meaning: The volume occupied by one mole of molecules of any gas at room temperature and pressure.
Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

items: Equal amounts in moles of gases occupy the same volume under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.
The volume of one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure is **24 dm³**.
24 dm³ is the same as 24 000 cm³.

blocks.label: Volume of a gas
where: volume is in dm³ (use 24 000 for cm³)
moles is the amount of gas in mol

blocks.label: Moles of a gas
where: moles is the amount of gas in mol
volume is in dm³ (divide cm³ by 1000)

items: One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ at room temperature and pressure.

sections.heading: Volume of a gas from its mass

blocks.text: Change the mass of a gas to moles using its Mr, then change moles to a volume.

items.text: Work out the relative formula mass of the gas.
Volume = moles × 24 dm³, or × 24 000 for cm³.

blocks.text: Example: the volume of 4.4 g of CO₂ at room temperature and pressure. Mr of CO₂ = 44. Moles = 4.4 ÷ 44 = 0.10 mol. Volume = 0.10 × 24 = 2.4 dm³ (2400 cm³).

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the volume of methane in cm³ from its mass at room temperature and pressure.
diagram.question: Calculate the volume of **{m}** g of methane, CH₄, at room temperature and pressure. Give your answer in cm³. Mr of CH₄ = 16. One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ (24 000 cm³).

items: Check the unit asked for. Multiply dm³ by 1000 to give cm³.

blocks.text: (Higher tier, chemistry only) The balanced equation gives the ratio of moles. For gases at the same temperature and pressure, it also gives the ratio of volumes.

items: In 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g), 20 cm³ of hydrogen reacts with 10 cm³ of oxygen.
Use the ratio directly when every volume is a gas at the same temperature and pressure.
If one substance is a solid or a liquid, go through moles: mass → moles → ratio → volume.

blocks.text: From a mass of solid to a volume of gas

items.text: Moles of the substance you know = mass ÷ Mr.
Use the equation to find the moles of the gas.

blocks.text: Example: 6.5 g of zinc (Ar = 65) in Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Moles of Zn = 0.10 mol, so moles of H₂ = 0.10 mol. Volume = 0.10 × 24 = 2.4 dm³.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the volume of oxygen made when hydrogen peroxide decomposes.
diagram.question: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂. **{m}** g of hydrogen peroxide (Mr = 34) decomposes completely. Calculate the volume of oxygen made at room temperature and pressure, in dm³.
working: 2 mol of H₂O₂ makes 1 mol of O₂, so moles of O₂ = moles of H₂O₂ ÷ 2.

blocks.text: From a volume of gas to a mass

items: Use the equation ratio to find the moles of the other substance.
Gases at the same temperature and pressure react in the ratio of the numbers in the equation.
For a solid or liquid, go through moles: mass → moles → ratio → volume.

checks.q: What is the volume of 0.50 mol of oxygen gas at room temperature and pressure?
Calculate the volume, in cm³, of 1.6 g of oxygen gas, O₂, at room temperature and pressure. Mr of O₂ = 32.
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. What volume of oxygen reacts with 60 cm³ of hydrogen, with all gas volumes at the same temperature and pressure?
checks.a: The ratio H₂ : O₂ is 2 : 1, so 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm³ of oxygen.

mistakes.wrong: Volume of 2.1 g of C₃H₆ = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 cm³.
mistakes.right: 0.05 × 24 gives dm³. Convert to cm³ by using 24 000 cm³ per mole: 0.05 × 24 000 = 1200 cm³. Use of no conversion loses the final mark.

mistakes.wrong: Moles of chlorine = moles of TiO₂ = 1250.
mistakes.right: Use the ratio in the equation. TiO₂ + 2Cl₂ means moles of Cl₂ = 1250 × 2 = 2500.

mistakes.wrong: Moles of TiO₂ = 100 ÷ 80, using 100 kg as the mass.
mistakes.right: Convert kg to g first: 100 kg = 100 000 g. Moles = 100 000 ÷ 80 = 1250.

worked_example.question:
C₃H₆ is a gas at room temperature and pressure. The volume of one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure is 24 dm³. Relative atomic masses (Ar): H = 1, C = 12.

Calculate the volume of 2.1 g of C₃H₆ at room temperature and pressure. Give your answer in cm³.
worked_example.tip: One mark each. The conversion from dm³ to cm³ can be done at any point in the method.

mistakes.wrong: Air contains 20% oxygen, so the volume of air = 400 × 20 ÷ 100 = 80 dm³.
mistakes.right: The oxygen is only 20% of the air, so the air is larger: 400 × 100 ÷ 20 = 2000 dm³.

mistakes.wrong: Mass of CO₂ from 75 mol of H₂ = 75 × 44 = 3300 g.
mistakes.right: Use the ratio. CH₄ + 2H₂O → 4H₂ + CO₂ gives 4 H₂ for each CO₂, so moles of CO₂ = 75 ÷ 4 = 18.75, and the mass is 18.75 × 44 = 825 g.

mistakes.wrong: Moles of CO₂ = 75 × 4 = 300 mol, giving 13 200 g.
mistakes.right: The ratio is the wrong way round. There are fewer moles of CO₂ than of H₂, so divide by 4.

worked_example.question:
In one stage of the production of nitric acid, nitrogen oxide, NO, is reacted with oxygen to make nitrogen dioxide, NO₂.

2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂

Calculate the minimum volume of air, measured at room temperature and pressure, required to react with 1000 g nitrogen oxide to form nitrogen dioxide.

Assume that the air contains 20% oxygen by volume.
(relative atomic masses: N = 14, O = 16
1 mol of gas occupies 24 dm³ at room temperature and pressure)
answer_points: Moles of O₂ = moles of NO ÷ 2 = 16.67 mol.
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 2000 dm³ scores all four marks. Stopping at 400 dm³ of oxygen loses the last mark.

exam_phrases: moles of CO = moles of CO2

mistakes.right: Hydrogen gas is H₂, so Mr = 2.0. Moles = 0.008 ÷ 2 = 0.004.
0.004 × 24 gives 0.096 dm³. The question asks for cm³, so multiply by 1000 to give 96 cm³.

mistakes.wrong: Moles of CO = 4.25 ÷ 2, because the equation has 2CO + 2NO.
mistakes.right: The ratio 2CO : 2CO₂ is 1 : 1, so moles of CO = moles of CO₂ = 4.25.

worked_example.question:
The equation shows the reaction that takes place in a catalytic converter.
2CO + 2NO → N₂ + 2CO₂

During a car journey, 187 g of carbon dioxide is made by the catalytic converter.

Calculate the volume of carbon monoxide, in dm³, removed from the exhaust gases.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): C = 12.0   O = 16.0
answer_points: Moles of CO = moles of CO₂ = 4.25 mol (a 1 : 1 ratio).
worked_example.tip: An answer of 102 dm³ scores all four marks. Find moles from the mass, use the ratio, then multiply by 24.
